claim: The pixel-size calibration cal-pixel-size-20260919 will not be repeated. The twelve values it produced are the ones in use, and no superseding measurement is planned.

valid_until.event: cal-pixel-size-20260919 is superseded by a new pixel-size calibration. The DATE IS NOT CHOSEN, it is inherited: this claim is about that calibration, so it cannot outlive the calibration's own outer bound, which is the operator's stated fifteen years anchored to 2026-09-19. A claim about a measurement that outlived the measurement would assert something about a number nobody is standing behind any more.

validity_conditions:
This instrument, the calibration cal-pixel-size-20260919 and the twelve entries it produced.

WHY IT IS FILED AT ALL. The question this answers -- what ends the twelve before 2041 -- has a recalibration as its most obvious answer, and a store that does not record the answer sends the next reader to ask the person a question he has already answered. That re-asking is the failure this repository keeps recording.

IT IS AN INTENT AND THE STORE HAS NO KIND FOR ONE. src_person_ruling_20260921 sets this out rather than hiding it: a ruling is defined as a judgement that new evidence overturns, and this is a decision the person can simply reverse. Filed under person_ruling because the alternatives are worse and inventing a source kind is not this seat's to do. WHAT FOLLOWS FOR A READER: do not treat this as a property of the instrument. If the person recalibrates, this entry is superseded by that event and not refuted by it -- the distinction rule 8 turns on.

SEPARATE FROM objective_change_selects_a_pixel_size_row, WHICH CAME FROM THE SAME SENTENCE ON THE SAME DAY. One claim per file (rule 1), and the test is independence: the person could recalibrate tomorrow, which would end this entry and leave the other standing untouched, because the objective indexing is a property of how the calibration was taken and not of whether it is redone.
